title: Snap CEO sidesteps Specs preorder questions on Q2 earnings call
summary: When asked about product-market fit, Spiegel said he believes mass-market consumer adoption won't occur until the end of the decade.
full_text:
Snap CEO Evan Spiegel sidestepped investors’ questions about preorder demand for the company’s long-awaited Specs smart glasses during Monday’s earnings call, just weeks before the device’s September launch event.
“What we’re hearing from folks is really that they want to try Specs,” Spiegel told investors. “It’s obviously a high consideration purchase at $2,195. Obviously, developers and folks who are familiar with the platform really understand it and understand the technical leaps we’ve made with this generation. I think for the broader public and consumers, it’s going to be really important for folks to go hands-on. Our upcoming launch event will be an important sort of starting point for that consumer-oriented journey.”
The company unveiled Specs in June after spending more than a decade developing the device. The wearable’s $2,195 price tag is significantly higher than most Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses, which start at around $350, but lower than Apple’s Vision Pro, which starts at $3,500.
Investors also pressed Spiegel on why he believes Snap’s strategy is financially viable for a company of its size, why it chose to go it alone rather than partner with another company, and what gives him confidence that the company can compete with Apple, Meta, and Alphabet.
Spiegel responded that Snap believes the long-term opportunity to develop the next computing platform is “enormous.”
“I think what some folks maybe don’t understand yet, especially because Specs are so new and we’re really the first mover in this category, is how difficult the product is to execute from a technical perspective,” Spiegel said. “When we started innovating in the social space, we were a late entrant. So, most of the apps at the time, whether it was Facebook or Instagram or Twitter, were already in existence, and we had to really innovate to continue to grow. What’s so unique about this opportunity for us is really that we’re a first mover, and that really plays to our strengths as an innovator.”
When asked about product-market fit, Spiegel said it will likely be closer to the end of the decade before the company sees mass-market consumer adoption.
“I think things, for example, like weight and cost are going to have to come down to see you know unit volumes really meaningfully pick up.” But we do have, I think, a real advantage here in that developers have been building on the Specs platform now for several years.”

title: Did an AI Music App Just Snitch on the Song of the Summer?
summary: Fenix Flexin’s hit song “Rubberz” has hip-hop fans arguing over whether it was generated by AI. Some say they have proof it’s machine-made, but will anyone care?
full_text:
There is no such thing as a universal “song of the summer” anymore, but if you’re into rap music, Fenix Flexin’s “Rubberz” is a pretty strong contender.
Officially released in June, it currently sits at #58 in the Billboard Hot 100 and has a music video with 7 million views. Lyrically, it’s got everything you’d want: boasts about cash and jewelry, and bars that work as a double entendre for braggadocio and depression.
But there are two interesting twists to “Rubberz.” First, it isn’t a rap song at all; it’s a synth-pop tune that would be at home in a moody ‘80s playlist. Also, since it dropped, it’s been the focus of accusations that it was completely or partially AI-generated.
The argument reached a peak this weekend after an independent music producer claimed he’d figured out not only how Fenix had made “Rubberz,” but that the rapper’s labelmate, Tyga, also seems to have used a little-known generative AI music app to create some ‘80s-themed tunes of his own.
And now, the creators of that same AI music app have effectively snitched on both: the service’s new built-in detector is now flagging the songs made by both Fenix and Tyga as likely AI generated.
This may finally settle the argument fans have been having all summer. It won’t settle the one they’re about to start.
Tune Up
People were suspicious of Fenix from the beginning; “Rubberz” is not only an unusual genre shift for the artist, it also doesn’t sound like his voice in the song.
Fenix Flexin grew up in East Hollywood and he sounds like it, and when he first debuted as part of the group Shoreline Mafia in the late 2010s, you could always recognize which bars were his because of his somewhat nasally, congested voice. The voice on his June 5 release of “Rubberz,” however, is completely unrecognizable. It’s a lot brighter and crisper, and the accent sounds closer to a very chipper Morrissey.
Both he and the credited producer, Purps on the Beat, have denied using AI at every turn. Fenix told Channel 5 that he “freestyled” the lyrics, and in the comments of an On the Radar performance, he replied to people accusing him of using AI: "No sirrrrrrr, recorded same as all music I do! Only difference is auto-tune reverb and me using my fake uk accent lol."
Not everyone bought his explanation, but there was no proof otherwise. As the summer continued, music media debated whether “Rubberz” had been AI-generated. But none of the well-known AI music detectors flagged it, Fenix denied it, and the song continued to rack up plays. Fans had no choice but to get comfortable with the question being unresolved.
Then, things shifted suddenly. On Thursday, a music producer named Medasin posted a video claiming he’d figured out how Fenix used AI to make the track.
It wasn’t Suno, or Udio, the two most prominent generative AI tools for making music. Instead, Medasin says, Flexin had used a lesser-known app called Treblo. Medasin breaks down his accusation methodically: first, he points out that the app used to be called Sonauto until two days before “Rubberz” was released. And then he shows a screencap of one of Fenix’s old Instagram Stories teasing his new ‘80s sound. A freeze-frame and zoom reveals that a filename being shown on screen has the suffix “Sonauto.mp3.”
But the most compelling accusation comes when Medasin shows how he was able to use Treblo to create a very similar track. By using tags like “80s synthwave” and prompting the app to write lyrics about a “rapper lifestyle,” Medasin got a similar-sounding song. The lyrics even bear more than a passing resemblance to “Rubberz.”
For example, Medasin’s prompt got him the lyrics “Diamond chains hanging heavy”; “Rubberz”’ has “Now I bought a heavy diamond chain.” Medasin’s generated song gave him “I see your face in the champagne bubbles”; Fenix’ song has “Still seeing your face in the glass.” Both songs feature some permutation of “pockets thick,” both mention “plastic smiles.”
“There's just way too many coincidences,” Medasin said in an interview with WIRED. “It is just a mathematical impossibility that he did not use Treblo.”
This all made me curious, though. Would Treblo allow me to recreate a “Rubberz”-style song? It turns out: yes.
By entering tags like “80s synthwave” and asking it to make rap lyrics, I got not only a similar sound, but similar lyrical structures.
In my first try, I generated a song (you can hear it here) with the couplet “Rings on every finger / Leather seats and cedar scent linger,” an almost mirror duplicate of the “Rubberz” line “Gold rings on my fingers / Still your perfume lingers.” I continued to generate songs. Even with slight variations, any time I combined an “80s” tag with a prompt for “rap lyrics,” I got similar results.
Whereas ChatGPT seems to like goblins, em dashes, and “It’s not X, it’s Y” constructions, Treblo’s engine seems to be obsessed with “finger/linger” rhyme pairs, talking about rings and glass and pockets, and song constructions in which there is a thematic transition from night into day.
Medasin says his Treblo revelation happened a month ago, but he kept it quiet; he figured some journalist would do the legwork of connecting the dots for the public. This did happen on a smaller scale, perhaps most thoroughly on an AI music news site called Zinstrel, but it never really broke through. Medasin’s video was the first to capture attention.
As Thursday went on, it seemed that Medasin had struck a nerve with his video accusation. That afternoon, Fenix posted a video on his Instagram page of what he said was the original project file for “Rubberz.” If authentic, this would serve as proof that the song was not AI; that “Rubberz” had been created from scratch in a studio.
But music producers immediately jumped into the comments, with many claiming that the project file being shown looked suspiciously like someone had just taken an existing song and used a “stem separator” to extract a full song into rudimentary components like bass and drums; which would point back to it just being an AI song that they couldn’t create.
Hours later, Fenix deleted the post. Neither he nor Purps On The Beat have addressed the “evidence” video since, or why it was taken down. Requests for comment sent to both by WIRED went unanswered.
Then, another one. Two days later on Saturday, Medasin dropped another video, this time alleging that Tyga’s new $TARFACE project is also at least partially using Treblo. He starts with some loose connections: videos were posted on social media of Tyga and Fenix together, both are on the same label, the same sudden rapper-to-80s crooner pathway. But also, he ran a Tyga song in a new AI music detector a friend is developing, and it was flagged as AI.
But it’s more convincing to hear directly from Treblo itself.
"Someone appears to have used our model to find a sound that millions of people connected with,” Treblo cofounder Ryan Tremblay said when asked for comment, “and that's exciting.”
Treblo had not previously spoken to Tyga or Fenix, Tremblay says, and the company wasn’t “even aware [“Rubberz”] existed until after it hit the Hot 100.”
Asking Treblo about individual songs might not be necessary in the future. Late Sunday night, Treblo published a page titled “Was This Made With Treblo?” In short, it’s a Treblo music detector. “We also think listeners should know what they're hearing,” a blog post explains, and describes it as a tool that is “tuned to detect songs made with Treblo with little to no modification.”
Sure enough, feeding “Rubberz” into the tool returns a result of “Very likely Treblo.” Running a track that Tyga dropped in early July returns a result of “Likely Treblo.”
The rate of false positives, Treblo’s site says, is under one in ten thousand; a fraction of a percent. The detector’s efficacy has not been independently reviewed, but Treblo has released the code under an open source license so anyone can inspect it and test it.

title: Rapists and child sex offenders to be barred from early release scheme
summary: The widow of PC Andrew Harper says it is "disgusting" her husband's killers remain eligible for the scheme in England and Wales.
full_text:
Rapists and child sex offenders to be barred from early release scheme
- Published
Prisoners who committed rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the forthcoming early release scheme for England and Wales, the government has said.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham paused plans to release some prisoners in September as part of a bid to stop unprecedented prison overcrowding after backlash from survivors and victims. The scheme will now restart in October.
Burnham said he "wanted to go even further", but that would not be possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".
Lissie Harper, the widow of police officer Andrew Harper, said it was "disgusting" that his killers could be eligible for early release.
PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of the quad bike theft in Berkshire.
His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) confirming the offenders who killed the officer could be included in the scheme.
Burnham had paused the scheme on 23 July to conduct an urgent review.
In a statement announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."
But Lissie Harper said that she was "beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear that Andrew's killers are soon to be free to roam the streets".
Under the government's changes, it also announced an extra £10 million will go to frontline victim support services, including a new national helpline.
The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.
The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.
Under Burnham's announced changes, rape and child sexual offences will now also be excluded.
The government said this move does not require changes to the existing legislation before October, though it may make amendments in the future to exclude certain offenders from being released.
Offenders of other crimes serving longer sentences of four years or more will be eligible for release halfway through their sentences rather than two-thirds as had previously been the case.
Those serving less serious sentences could be freed after a third of their time, rather than half.
The changes are due to be phased in, beginning with prisoners serving sentences of less than 575 days, going up to inmates jailed for 12 years or more being eligible for early release in June 2027.
The "presumption" will be that offenders are tagged and will face longer periods of supervision and tough new rules including "restriction zones", Burnham said.
The number of individuals released each time will depend on the make-up of the prison population, which the government says will evolve between now and implementation.
Reacting to the announcement, a prison officer told the BBC that they were "creaking at the seams" and that "delaying the releases until October could mean we simply run out of space".
A probation officer said it is "not clear there's anything actually new here in terms of how probation staff are going to manage people being released earlier".
Separately, those who serve the full sentence and are convicted of rape or serious child sex offences will face stronger surveillance after leaving prison, the government said.
This includes 12 months of GPS monitoring and strengthened community supervision.
Calling the announcement a "U-turn", Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy said it "doesn't go far enough".
"Some child sex offenders and killers ... will still be released early. And the trauma of victims being told their abusers may be released can't be undone," he said.
Domestic Abuse Commissioner Dame Nicole Jacobs criticised the decision to not exclude domestic abuse perpetrators.
"It is critical that no abuser is released in October unless I am confident that victims' safety is not being compromised," she said.

title: EU calls for stronger borders after Ceuta migrant crossings
summary: Ursula von der Leyen has called for action ahead of an urgent EU interior ministers meeting to discuss the issue.
full_text:
EU calls for stronger borders after Ceuta migrant crossings
- Published
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called for "united action" on border security after the chaotic influx of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta last week.
Spain estimates that about 69,500 migrants have now returned to Morocco, exceeding initial estimates of 50,000. The official death toll on the Spanish side of the border stands at 72, with 11 deaths on the Moroccan side.
On Tuesday, EU interior ministers will have emergency talks by video conference to discuss the issue.
The scenes in Ceuta have strained relations among some of the EU's 27 member states.
In a letter to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, von der Leyen praised his "swift handling" of the crisis.
But she added: "From this incident, it is clear that we must do more to further strengthen our borders at critical points."
In response to the Ceuta crossings, Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen arrangement with Spain.
The Schengen agreement eliminates border checks and now encompasses more than 450 million people and 29 countries in Europe.
Finland and Denmark backed Italy's move, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain's Schengen membership.
In response, Sánchez said he had "serious concerns" about some European governments and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area.
While most had shown "support and solidarity", he said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, "driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest".
In her letter to the Spanish PM, von der Leyen warned that "the protection of all our external borders is a shared European responsibility", while calling for "vigilant monitoring and the use of physical barriers where needed".
Tuesday's video conference will be a chance to draw "lessons" from the Ceuta episode, von der Leyen said, warning the challenges of illegal immigration require "a common European response, united action and solidarity".
She urged the EU to "double down" in five areas: preventing irregular migration in the first place via cooperation with partner states; strengthening external borders; implementing early warning systems; dismantling smuggling networks and reinforcing returns.
Sánchez has accused migrant traffickers of exploiting a decision recently made by the country's supreme court which constrained the government's right to immediately deport people who had arrived by sea.
The country's Interior Minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said on Saturday that the situation had almost returned to normal and the country was working on an inflatable barrier to prevent illegal migration via the water.

title: US reports first two deaths linked to  'explosive diarrhoea' outbreak
summary: The illness caused by parasitic infection that spreads through contaminated food or water is not generally life-threatening, health officials say.
full_text:
US reports first two deaths linked to 'explosive diarrhoea' outbreak
- Published
Michigan health officials have confirmed the first two deaths linked to the ongoing cyclospora outbreak, a parasitic infection spread through contaminated food or water that can cause severe diarrhoea.
The two individuals had "significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration", state health authorities said.
The foodborne illness has spread to 45 states, with nearly 7,000 laboratory-confirmed cases reported nationwide, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
While the outbreak has infected thousands of people, the CDC says deaths from cyclosporiasis are far from common, as it is "not usually life-threatening".
Michigan's health department did not provide further details about those who have died.
The state is at the epicentre of the current outbreak and its records show more than 11,000 cases and 193 hospitalisations, although many have not been laboratory-confirmed.
The heat-loving parasite infects the intestines and is transmitted through faecal contamination.
Past outbreaks have occurred when people consumed fruits or vegetables irrigated with water contaminated by faeces.
The CDC recommends washing all produce under running water, including those that are labelled as pre-washed.
But washing alone might not be enough to rid produce of the parasite. Cooking produce to a temperature of at least 70°C (158 °F) can kill the parasite, the agency recommends.
Officials have linked this year's widespread outbreak to lettuce imported from Taylor Farms in Mexico, a key supplier for many food establishments in the US.
US fast-food chain Taco Bell said it has removed lettuce from the supplier from its menu. Taylor Farms itself announced a voluntary recall of lettuce sourced from central Mexico.
UK health officials too have warned about the outbreak following recent cases contracted by returning travellers.

title: From Trump to El-Sayed: US Arabs in Michigan centre Palestine in politics
summary: Arab Americans in Michigan who withheld support for Kamala Harris in 2024 say they will not back pro-Israel candidates.

From Trump to El-Sayed: US Arabs in Michigan centre Palestine in politics
Arab Americans in Michigan who withheld support for Kamala Harris in 2024 say they will not back pro-Israel candidates.
Dearborn, Michigan – Yemeni-American activist Samraa Luqman has no regrets about voting for President Donald Trump in 2024.
While the United States president has been a disappointment to Arab Americans in Michigan with his pro-war and anti-immigration policies, she stressed that it was untenable for the community to vote for Democrats as Israel’s genocide unfolded in Gaza.

“There had to be accountability for the genocide. We’re OK with what we voted for,” Luqman told Al Jazeera.
“I said from the beginning, I’m willing to live through another four years of Trump, that we expected him to be bad on our issues, but it was a pill we were willing to swallow in order to hold the Democratic Party accountable.”
Luqman is not alone.
Despite Trump’s staunchly pro-Israel policies and unpopular war on Iran, many say supporting Democratic nominee Kamala Harris in 2024 was out of the question, and it was the right choice for the community to break with the Democratic Party.
“I could not – with a good heart, good conscience – tell someone to vote for Kamala Harris or Donald Trump”, but the approach of “lesser of two evils” no longer works to sway Arab voters, Hussein Dabajeh, a prominent political strategist in the Detroit area, home to large Arab and Muslim communities, told Al Jazeera.
Democrats’ popularity amongst Arab Americans nosedived in 2024 as President Joe Biden ignored calls to compel a ceasefire in Gaza and continued to provide Israel with weapons and military aid as it killed tens of thousands in Palestine and Lebanon.
Then, Vice President Harris refused even to consider an arms embargo against Israel.
As a result of these policies, many Arab Americans, who had been reliable Democratic voters for years, ditched the party and refused to support Harris in her presidential bid.
Trump swept in, presented himself as a “peace” candidate, and his campaign forged ties with Arab community advocates.
Trump’s policies
At a rally in Michigan ahead of the 2024 vote, Trump brought local Muslim imams to the stage and praised the community.
The Republican leader also visited the predominantly Arab and Muslim Detroit suburb of Dearborn ahead of the election.
Trump ended up winning Michigan as many Arab voters in the Dearborn area refused to back Harris. Some voted for him, while others voted for a third party, left the top of the ticket blank, or skipped the election altogether.
According to an Al Jazeera analysis of election results in heavily Arab precincts in east Dearborn, about 45 percent of the votes went to Trump, 29 percent to Green Party candidate Jill Stein, and 16 percent to Harris.
As president, Trump allowed Israel to continue its attacks on Gaza and Lebanon and launched an unprovoked war against Iran that has sent petrol prices soaring.
He has also intensified the crackdown on Palestinian rights advocacy at home with a campaign to deport noncitizen student activists critical of Israel.
In February, he also terminated immigration protections for Yemeni nationals, sowing fear and uncertainty in a community where many leaders had endorsed him in 2024.
Asked how Arab Americans feel about Trump now, Dabajeh said: “They hate him. There’s no other way of putting it. I don’t think there is a single person I know that voted for Trump from the Arab and Muslim community specifically that looks at what Trump is doing and is happy with what he’s doing, or what he’s done.”
‘The genocide matured us’
Many Arab Americans stress that withholding support for Harris in 2024 was not out of love for Trump.
“No one understands the horrors of Trump’s policy more than us. We were his first victims in 2017,” said Amer Zahr, a comedian and Dearborn Board of Education trustee.
Shortly after starting his first term in 2017, Trump implemented a travel ban on several Muslim-majority countries.
“No one is more aware of the harm that Trump can cause than we are,” Zahr added. “But the genocide matured us in a way that we finally got to the point where we were willing to tell politicians ‘no’.”
As the election season returns to Michigan, Arab Americans once again find themselves at a political crossroads.
The community is rallying behind Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed – who had previously endorsed Harris – but some are keeping their political options open.
Luqman, the Yemeni activist, said she will certainly vote for El-Sayed and Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib – who are outspoken critics of Israel – in the Democratic primary on Tuesday and in the general elections in November.
Luqman said Democratic voters’ support for progressive candidates will help the party regain credibility with Arab voters.
“Those are things that do bring the Democratic Party a little bit of relevance and credibility within our community,” Luqman told Al Jazeera.
“It has kind of brought the community back to centre, whereas they were kind of swinging to the right by a large margin.”
Palestine or bust
While some political commentators have been questioning why US support for Israel has become a decisive issue in US politics, particularly Democratic primaries, the answer in the Arab community is clear.
Advocates say domestic policy takes a backseat when their loved ones are being killed, and their hometowns are being wiped out by their own tax dollars via military aid to Israel.
“Gaza and Palestine and Middle Eastern issues have now become the forefront, the top of everybody’s issues, and it’s become a red line for my community,” Luqman said.
“So if you’re a Republican or Democrat and you hate AIPAC and you value Palestinians’ rights to self-determination, then you’re going to be getting our vote, regardless of what party you’re in,” she said, referencing the powerful American Israel Public Affairs Committee lobby group.
Zahr echoed that message.
“People want us not to be single-issue voters. In other words, they want us to forgo our main issue, get screwed on it, watch our families die because Trump’s bad, and accept all that,” he said.
“Well, we said ‘no’. The blood of the children of Gaza had to mean something.”
Zahr emphasised that Arab Americans are not alone in centring Palestine in their electoral choices, pointing to the defeats that pro-Israel incumbents have suffered across the map in this primary season.
“You’ve gotten to a point where if somebody says, ‘Stop bombing hospitals’, everyone knows you’re talking about Israel. That’s because of Israel. That’s not because of us. That’s because of what Israel did,” he told Al Jazeera.
“And so, people are keying into the truth. And when you learn the truth, something that comes along with that is you learn that you’ve been lied to, and you get angry. A lot of righteous anger is pushing a lot of this.”
Dabajeh, the political strategist, said that while Arab voters care about the economy, affordability and infrastructure – like all Americans – they cannot overlook US policy on Israel.
“Are we supposed to call our family members overseas and be like, ‘Listen, khalto [auntie], this guy over here that’s running for office might kill some of your neighbours, might kill some of your kids, but don’t worry about it, he’s going to take care of the flooding in our homes’?”
“It’s not going to work. We can’t do that.”

Tennis: Philippines’ Eala wins first WTA title, Fritz claims DC crown
Alex Eala rallies past top seed Jessica Pegula in a two-day, rain-hit final, while Taylor Fritz beats teen Rafael Jodar.
Alexandra Eala made history as the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour-level singles title, defeating top seed Jessica Pegula at the Mubadala DC Open before Taylor Fritz claimed the men’s crown.
The 21-year-old Eala rallied to beat world number three Pegula 4-6, 6-4, 6-0 in a weather-disrupted women’s final that spanned two days, ending on Monday.

Rain had suspended play on Sunday with Pegula leading by a set but trailing 2-1 in the second. Upon Monday’s resumption, Eala dominated, winning 10 of the final 13 games with aggressive baseline play and a formidable serve to seal her breakthrough victory.

My first chance at a title, knowing it won’t be the last, and already having achieved this milestone for my career,” Eala said on the court after lifting the trophy in front of a vocal contingent of supporters. “I knew whatever happened after this match would have already been a win for me.”

“To see how far you’ve come over the last couple of years… to see the amazing fans that follow you every place you go, it’s not fun to play against, but I think it’s amazing,” Pegula told Eala during the trophy presentation.

Fritz, returning to peak form following a knee injury that sidelined him earlier this season, produced a steady performance behind his serve, winning 81 percent of his first-serve points.

The double bill concluded a rain-plagued week in the US capital as players now head into the North American hardcourt swing ahead of the US Open.

title: These are some of the last pristine ocean ecosystems. Now, they're losing protections
summary: The largest conservation areas in the U.S. are in the Pacific Ocean, where tiny islands are epicenters of biodiversity. The Trump administration is now opening their waters to commercial fishing, sparking a battle over some of the country's most pristine ecosystems.
full_text:
Some of the most pristine ecosystems left in the world are found in the Pacific.
Troubled Waters
The largest conservation areas in the U.S. are in the Pacific Ocean. President Trump is rolling back their protections.
Reporting by Lauren Sommer
Visuals by Claire Harbage
This story was supported by the Pulitzer Center.
Published Aug. 3, 2026
These remote islands and atolls are biodiversity hot spots, home to thriving coral reefs …
… and bustling seabird colonies.
More than a million square miles of the Pacific Ocean are safeguarded as U.S. marine national monuments and sanctuaries.
Now, the Trump administration is opening some of these waters to commercial fishing.
Thousands of miles from California, the Pacific marine monuments are centered on tiny islands and atolls.
One of them is Palmyra Atoll, about as far from a continent as you can get on the planet.
No one lives here permanently, but it’s home to a field research station run by The Nature Conservancy, a conservation nonprofit. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service staff also rotate in, since the atoll’s land is protected as a national wildlife refuge.
For the researchers and staff stationed here, some days their closest neighbors are the astronauts passing overhead in the International Space Station.
For decades, scientists have studied Palmyra Atoll’s unique ecosystem, a window into the vital role that atolls play for marine life across the Pacific.
“Atolls are small when you look at them on the map, but they have an oversized impact on the ocean around them,” says Alex Wegmann, lead scientist of island resilience at The Nature Conservancy.
“They are very important epicenters of biodiversity and of abundance.”
Atolls are formed by ancient volcanic islands surrounded by coral reefs. As the volcano erodes and disappears below the water, the reef continues to grow upward.
Eventually a ring of low-lying islands forms, built from the skeletons of the reef that surrounds it.
For millennia, Pacific atolls were important stopover and cultural sites for Polynesians who crossed the Pacific Ocean on seafaring voyages.
Colonial powers reshaped many atolls, removing native forests to plant fast-growing coconut palm plantations. Although many were abandoned, the palms continued to spread, crowding out native trees.
World War II brought even more changes. As fighting in the Pacific escalated, the U.S. military remade many atolls, building bunkers, air bases and refueling stations. Ship channels were dredged through coral reefs. Some atolls were used for nuclear and biological weapons testing.
Still, Pacific atolls remain among the wildest places on the planet.
Seabirds use them as nesting sites to raise their young, returning to the open ocean to hunt for fish. Sooty terns spend years at sea, flying thousands of miles before coming back to land to breed.
The reefs surrounding many atolls are still largely untouched, with coral colonies the size of city buses.
At Palmyra Atoll, blacktip and grey reef sharks cruise the reefs’ edges. Scientists have found it has one of the highest densities of predators in the world, a rare example of a food chain that remains intact.
Pacific atolls also attract deep-water species that swim hundreds of miles, like tuna. In the warm, nutrient-poor waters of the central Pacific where food is sparse, atolls are like bustling cafés.
Scientists put satellite tags on yellowfin tuna, tracking where they swam for months, and found they congregate around atolls.
Seabirds rely on those tuna and other large predators to corral schools of small fish. As tuna feed, they drive the schools near the ocean’s surface, where birds can reach them.
This interconnected ecosystem, stretching from treetops to the deep sea, is one of the reasons the waters around Pacific atolls were granted federal protections.

title: House Ethics panel recommends censure for Chuck Edwards after harassment allegations
summary: After a months-long investigation, the ethics committee recommended censure for Edwards because of "persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."
full_text:
House Ethics panel recommends censure for Chuck Edwards after harassment allegations
The House Ethics Committee is recommending that Rep. Chuck Edwards be censured because of "persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."
The committee has been investigating the North Carolina Republican for months and published its 20-page report on Monday.
The bipartisan committee said it did not find evidence that the congressman propositioned his staffers or engaged in sexual activity with them.
The report states that in his interview with the committee, Edwards asserted he understood "sexual harassment."
"[He] seemed to believe that by avoiding inappropriate physical touch, explicitly sexual comments, and occasionally telling staffers that they were free to put up boundaries with him, he had immunized himself from such a charge," the report reads. "That is not the case."
The panel investigated allegations that Edwards, who took office in 2023, may have created a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment.
Edwards' office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a rebuttal to the committee's report, lawyers for the congressman said the panel had failed to demonstrate that the staffers expressed their discomfort to Edwards.
"Representative Edwards has been denied the opportunity to challenge the factual allegations guaranteed to him under House rules," they wrote in their response. They also said the congressman "sincerely regrets that his behavior created discomfort" for either of the two staffers.
The investigation details his interactions with two young female staffers, including showering them with "lavish and recurrent gifts," including jewelry totaling over $1,000, designer purses, guns, shoes, flowers, a laptop and cell phone, KitchenAid mixer, vacations and one-on-one-dinners.
The report also found that the congressman made comments regarding these staffers' appearances, invited them to intimate dinners and vacations, and sent them notes "regarding his effusive affection."
The report said both women attempted to communicate their discomfort with their boss's behavior, and that ultimately, a senior staffer spoke to Edwards on their behalf.
That staffer testified that Edwards, 65, said she "didn't understand the unique relationship" he had with them.
Edwards cooperated with the committee's investigation, which included 16 witness interviews, including the congressman himself, and over 1,500 pages of evidence.
The committee voted to issue this report on July 22.
The House is currently on recess, so the censure itself would not take place until at least September. A censure is the strongest punishment the panel can recommend short of expulsion. It is tantamount to a public shaming on the House floor.

My view is that China’s military has made tremendous progress in the process of modernisation over the last 10 years. If we talk about history, what does it mean in modern military history? This is a very big moment. China has said for a long time it wants to be a world-leading military, a world-class military. There are areas where there’s now emerged a big discrepancy between China and other countries, and ultimately that does hurt China because there is fear. You can sense it in the region. There’s quite a palpable anxiety about where the region is going in a world where clearly the United States is playing less of a role and China is playing much more of a role.

title: What We Know About the Suspected Idaho In-N-Out Shooter—and the Bystanders Credited With Distracting Him
summary: Authorities commended two bystanders for intervening during the shooting, saying that “their heroic actions” likely helped prevent more people from being injured in the incident.
full_text:
Three victims died and seven others were injured on Saturday, after a man began shooting at an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho. Police said the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Shortly before 2:30 p.m. on Saturday, the Twin Falls Police Department received multiple 911 calls about shots fired near the fast food restaurant, which had just opened in Twin Falls the week before.
Of the seven people who were injured, two have received treatment and have been released from the hospital; three are in stable condition; and two are in critical condition, the Twin Falls Police Department said on Sunday. Authorities said the same day that they weren’t sharing the identities of the victims at the moment, out of respect for the families, some of whom had not yet been notified.
Lynsi Snyder, the president of In-N-Out, revealed in a social media post on Sunday that one of the victims who was killed in the shooting was a restaurant employee. She didn’t share the name of the employee, but said that the restaurant “lost one of our beautiful Associates.”
“She was taking care of our most important asset—our Customers, and her life was taken by a disgusting human who doesn’t value the lives of others or his own,” Snyder said. “He shot both on our property and off, and ended his life shortly after he took the precious lives of our Associate and Customers, innocent people who never saw it coming.”
“IN-N-OUT will be mourning with the families and praying for them as they tread through a very painful season,” Snyder continued.
While authorities were conducting their search for the suspect on Saturday, an officer-involved shooting occurred, but police said no one was wounded and they didn’t share further details about the incident.
Authorities also credited two bystanders with intervening during the shooting, saying that “their heroic actions” likely helped prevent more people from being injured in the incident.
Little information has so far been shared about the suspect and about the bystanders, who authorities have not publicly identified. Here’s what we know about them so far.
Who was the shooter?
The Twin Falls Police Department identified the suspect as a 24-year-old man named Chad Williams. While the authorities didn’t share any details about a possible motive for the shooting, they said that they “are confident the suspect acted alone.”
“Investigators are continuing to review evidence, conduct interviews, and determine the full circumstances, including possible motivation,” the department said in a social media post on Sunday.
Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said at a press conference on Sunday that the suspect’s family was cooperating with investigators.
Police also dispelled misinformation that had been circulating online about the suspect’s identity, saying that some social media posts had erroneously identified a different individual as the suspect. Authorities urged the public not to share any unconfirmed information about the shooting.
Who are the bystanders who intervened?
The Twin Falls Police Department said that two bystanders—an off-duty state trooper and a private citizen—”returned gunfire toward the suspect” during the shooting on Saturday.
Authorities didn’t release the identities of the bystanders, but thanked them for intervening.
“We commend their heroic actions, which we believe helped drive the suspect away from the scene and prevent further casualties,” the department said in its social media post.
One of the bystanders came forward to share his account of the incident with the Idaho Statesman. Jordan Salinas and his girlfriend were driving into the In-N-Out for lunch on Saturday when they saw people running out of the restaurant and heard gunshots. Salinas told the news outlet that his “automatic” response was to run toward the building, pulling out his semi-automatic pistol.
Salinas, who cares for his wheelchair-bound brother full-time, told the Idaho Statesman that he took firearm training seriously after a shooting occurred at the Boise Towne Square mall five years ago. He worried that shooters would target a person in a wheelchair.
On Saturday, he saw the suspect near the In-N-Out drive-through window, shooting at nearby cars. Salinas fired at the suspect.
“He did not like it when bullets started firing both ways,” Salinas told the Idaho Statesman.
He told the news outlet that he wasn’t afraid during the shooting, thinking to himself “there’s a task that needs to be done, and we’re the ones who need to do it.” When officers responded to the scene, Salinas stepped back so that they could take over.
“My part,” he recounted thinking, “is done."

title: Two People Have Died in the Cyclospora Outbreak
summary: Two people in Michigan “with significant underlying health conditions” died from complications of cyclosporiasis, state officials said.
full_text:
Two people in Michigan have died from cyclosporiasis, state health officials announced on Aug. 3. They are the first reported deaths from a record Cyclospora outbreak that has sickened thousands of people across the U.S.
“The reported deaths are a sobering reminder that cyclosporiasis is usually not life-threatening, but it can become very serious in vulnerable individuals,” says Rodney E. Rohde, chair of the Medical Laboratory Science Program at Texas State University.
The two people who died had “significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration,” according to an update on the Michigan health department’s website. The health department said it wouldn’t provide additional information on the two cases.
The U.S. is experiencing the largest Cyclospora outbreak in its recorded history, with more than 18,000 cases confirmed or suspected across 45 states since May 1, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Michigan, which has been particularly hard-hit by the pathogen, is at the center of a multi-state spate of cases linked to shredded iceberg lettuce. More than 11,200 cases of cyclosporiasis have been reported in the state since June 22, and more than 190 people have been hospitalized, according to Michigan officials.
Cyclospora is a parasite that spreads through human feces, typically via contaminated food and water. It can cause frequent, watery, and explosive diarrhea that can last days or weeks. More than 400 people have been hospitalized from cyclosporiasis across the country since the outbreak began, according to the CDC. Deaths from the parasite are uncommon in the U.S., food-safety experts say.
“While most people recover from cyclosporiasis, individuals with underlying medical conditions or those in higher-risk groups may be more susceptible to serious complications, especially if prolonged diarrhea results in dehydration,” says Wade Syers, a food-safety specialist at Michigan State University Extension. “Anyone experiencing persistent diarrhea, signs of dehydration, or worsening symptoms should seek medical attention, particularly if they are in a higher-risk group.”
People who are elderly or have weakened immune systems, including people who are undergoing chemotherapy or who have advanced HIV, are at greater risk of cyclosporiasis complications, says Rohde. Early diagnosis and treatment with antibiotics, along with aggressive fluid replacement when needed, can significantly reduce the risks of complications, he says.
To reduce potential exposure to Cyclospora, food-safety experts recommend buying intact heads of lettuce and whole fruits and vegetables over bagged, boxed, or pre-cut produce. They also advise people to wash produce thoroughly under running water and follow other food-safety best practices, such as keeping raw meat and vegetables separate when preparing and cooking food. Cooking food to an internal temperature of at least 158°F can kill Cyclospora.
Rohde says people should follow food-safety guidance to keep themselves safe from foodborne illnesses, but for most healthy people, “these deaths should increase awareness, not panic,” he says.

title: Your Fitbit data can now connect directly to Apple Health
summary: Google is rolling out an update that will finally allow you to connect your Fitbit workouts, steps, vitals, and other data to Apple Health, as reported earlier by 9to5Mac. With Google Health's 5.05 update, you can now tap your profile icon, select "Partner apps," and choose Apple Health to link your data directly. Previously, you […]
full_text:
Google is rolling out an update that will finally allow you to connect your Fitbit workouts, steps, vitals, and other data to Apple Health, as reported earlier by 9to5Mac. With Google Health’s 5.05 update, you can now tap your profile icon, select “Partner apps,” and choose Apple Health to link your data directly.
Your Fitbit data can now connect directly to Apple Health
Google Health can sync your workouts, steps, and vitals to Apple Health.
Previously, you could only import your Apple Health data into Google Health, but not the other way around. That meant using third-party apps — like Power Sync for Fitbit or Fitbit to Apple Health Sync — or some other kind of workaround to connect your Google Health information to Apple Health.
Google Health replaced the Fitbit app in May. The new app had a bit of a rocky rollout after users raised concerns over the new AI health coach, user interface, and other issues, though Google has since addressed some of these complaints.
Along with this update, Google announced that users in the US can use Smart Health Links to share medical records with a provider or family member. You can create a link by heading to the Health tab, choosing the “Medical” section, selecting “Shareable records,” and tapping the “plus” icon. From there, you can choose which data you want to include in the link and share it via a URL or QR code.

title: Samsung’s discounted smart monitor is $349.99, its lowest price yet
summary: Samsung makes a variety of TVs and computer monitors, but if want both and you’re limited on space, you might want to consider the M80F. This capable 32-inch 4K panel combines features commonly found on both types of screens, and Amazon and B&H Photo both have it discounted to $349.99, where it’s usually $400 or […]
full_text:
Samsung makes a variety of TVs and computer monitors, but if want both and you’re limited on space, you might want to consider the M80F. This capable 32-inch 4K panel combines features commonly found on both types of screens, and Amazon and B&H Photo both have it discounted to $349.99, where it’s usually $400 or much higher. In addition to acting as a standard 4K screen for your computer or console, the M80F has a full suite of video streaming apps you’d expect to find on a television, with picture-in-picture support for multitasking, plus a removable webcam for video chats.
Samsung’s discounted smart monitor is $349.99, its lowest price yet
This 4K smart monitor is loaded with features like streaming apps, cloud gaming apps, and a webcam.
The M80F has above-average connectivity for a monitor. In addition to the ports like HDMI 2.0, USB-C for charging devices up to 65W, and USB-A for your keyboard and mouse, you can also connect the Tizen interface to Wi-Fi to directly communicate with your network (it also supports Bluetooth headphones). Speaking of gaming, the M80F supports apps like Xbox and Nvidia GeForce Now, letting you pair a controller to the display to play games over the cloud. The VA panel is better suited for work than play, but HDR10 Plus support will help your movies and TV shows pop.
My colleague Cameron Faulkner reviewed a previous version of the M80F and appreciated its versatility, but the $699.99 launch price was a bit off-putting, so a discount on a newer, improved model is definitely worth calling out.
